description: Neptunium is a radioactive actinide metal with atomic number 93, representing the first transuranic element. It is named after Neptune, the planet beyond Uranus in the Solar System. A neptunium atom has 93 protons and 93 electrons, with seven valence electrons.
uses: Neptunium is used as a precursor for the formation of plutonium-238, which is employed in radioisotope thermal generators to provide electricity for spacecraft. It has also been used in detectors of high-energy neutrons.
characteristics: Neptunium metal is silvery and tarnishes when exposed to air, forming a thin oxide layer. The element is hard, ductile, and radioactive, with a melting point of 639 ± 3 °C and exhibits five oxidation states ranging from +3 to +7. Like all actinides, it is poisonous, pyrophoric, and capable of accumulating in bones, occurring in at least three allotropic forms.
